    common_pattern = re.compile(r'^(.+)\.s3[.\-][a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-[0-9]{1,}'
                                r'\.amazonaws\.com(\.[a-z]+)?$')
    # matches dualstack endpoints like
    #     - <bucket_name>.s3.dualstack.<region>.amazonaws.com'
    #     - <bucket_name>.s3.dualstack.<region>.amazonaws.com.cn'
    dualstack_pattern = re.compile(r'^(.+)\.s3\.dualstack\.[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-[0-9]{1,}'
                                   r'\.amazonaws\.com(\.[a-z]+)?$')
    # matches legacy endpoints like
    #     - '<bucket_name>.s3.amazonaws.com'
    #     - '<bucket_name>.s3-external-1.amazonaws.com.cn'
    legacy_patterns = re.compile(r'^(.+)\.s3\.?(-external-1)?\.amazonaws\.com(\.[a-z]+)?$')

    # if any of the above patterns match, the first captured group
    # will be returned as the bucket name
    host = headers['host']
    for pattern in [common_pattern, dualstack_pattern, legacy_patterns]:

        if match:

    # or a pattern matched the host and we're returning that name instead
    return normalize_bucket_name(bucket_name)

The error happens in `fix_range_content_type` (line 502-510), which calls `get_key_name(path, headers)` to extract the S3 object key from the request path. 

`get_key_name` (line 882) splits the path into parts and decides whether to return `path_parts[1]` (the key, path-style addressing) or `path_parts[0]` (just the key, virtual-hosted style) based on `uses_path_addressing()`.

`uses_path_addressing` checks if the host starts with `localhost`, `localhost.localstack.cloud`, or `127.0.0.1`. The `x-localstack-edge` header (set by the edge router) overrides the `host` header. On CircleCI, the host is a Docker container IP like `172.20.0.5`, so `uses_path_addressing` returns `False`. Then `get_key_name` incorrectly returns `path_parts[0]` (the bucket name) instead of `path_parts[1]` (the actual key). This causes `head_object(Bucket='test-bucket', Key='test-bucket')` → `HEAD /test-bucket/test-bucket`.

The fix needed is in `get_key_name`: when the path has more than one part (i.e., `/bucket/key`), we should always return the key part regardless of what `uses_path_addressing` returns.
